latest_final: Kameda and Umio were adversaries in a nonphysical struggle, and Kameda was deliberately reduced to literal fragments. Although Umio initially showed no damage, observers thought he was probably the loser because the struggle had a concrete consequence for him: an authority’s action worsened his physical health. The later chemical-weapon attack was a separate attempt to kill Umio, and was not the consequence observers relied on. The election connection was not relevant to why the men came into conflict. The clues do not identify the separate health consequence or explain the circumstances behind it, so that key part of the story remains unresolved.
